# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per

  the isolated `MessagingRepository` interface (send/peek/drain/directory —
  future DB/network impls drop in without caller changes).
  `AgentMessage.kind` distinguishes agent chat from `user` input handed
  over by an attached client (the Fa app's attach view; the CLI delivers
  it as `[from app] …`, its own words, not agent chat).
  `FileMessagingRepository` over `ExecutionEnv`:
  `<root>/<agent>/inbox|read/<id>.json`, timestamp-ordered names, sanitized
  agent dirs, torn writes skipped. `SubagentManager.messaging` routes
  `enqueueMessage`/`drainMessages` through the fabric (in-memory queue is
  the no-fabric fallback); `mailboxPrefix` (the session id, set by the host
  on every session init/switch) namespaces mailboxes so two instances never
  drain each other — ids with `/` are absolute cross-instance addresses
  (`<sessionId>/main`). Sessions also carry their display NAME
  (`--session goal_builder`): `register(agentId, {sessionName})` persists
  it in a `.name` marker + messages-registry.json, `agent_directory`
  renders `name (id)`, and `agent_message` resolves `goal_builder` /
  `goal_builder/main` through the directory (exact ids/siblings/`main`
  pass through untouched; ambiguous names error with candidates).
  `agent_message` targets siblings, `main`, a session name, or an
  absolute mailbox; `agent_directory` lists LIVE fabric mailboxes (recent
  activity via the heartbeat hosts touch on their inbox-watch timers) plus
  anything with pending mail — stale mailboxes from finished sessions are
  hidden behind the tool's `all: true` (`.id` markers keep real ids despite
  dir sanitization; `_scheduled`/dot-dirs are not mailboxes).
  `schedule_message` (issue #59): records under `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/`;
  self-addressed records deliver to the host's LIVE mailbox at fire time
  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those
  deliver as recorded (the address rides the same owner prefix and is as
  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)
  makes a subagent's no-`to` schedule default to the CHILD's mailbox, not
  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.
  gh-1180: a re-addressed SELF record also delivers FROM the live mailbox
  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2097): auto-compact measures honestly — no more stale pre-run
  estimates or «0 freed» basis flips. (1) `StructuredCompactor.run()`
  re-anchors the agent state from the session projection BEFORE any
  trigger/before/over math: the in-memory transcript can lag the session
  file (an in-memory tail cut, a second writer appending to the same
  session between runs), and the stale basis computed `over` ≈ 1.4k
  where ~177k was needed — the deterministic hide under-sized every
  pass and the run paid extra passes/minutes; one projection build
  bounded by the ledger cache (O(changed records)) now starts every
  run. (2) Pass reports render an upward basis jump explicitly:
  `StructuredCompactionPass`/`AutoCompactorPass` gain `basisReadTokens`
  (a pass appends only shrinkers, so an after-count above its
  before-count is a second writer's records entering the projection,
  never a regression) and `formatCompactionReport` prints
  `basis re-read: +Nk` instead of a clamped `0 freed · 0%`; the small
  restamp jitter (no flip metadata) keeps its `0 freed` clamp. (3) The
  compaction hooks' diagnostic lines (`auto-compact pass/retry/done`)
  now carry `sid=` like every other compaction lifecycle line, and the
  diagnostic appends run through one serialized in-order chain
  (`flushDiagnosticLog()`, awaited by the REPL teardown and the
  headless finally) — bursts land complete instead of being dropped by
  unawaited fire-and-forget appends racing the process exit. AC: a
  two-writer fixture asserts correct first-pass sizing; golden tests
  pin the basis-flip rendering; log tests pin sid presence and
  no-dropped-lines. (4) The app's over-window relief
  (`AgentService._relieveOverWindow`) now drains the pending persist
  BEFORE compacting — the same ordering the run-end funnel and the CLI
  already enforce: the structured engine's run-start re-anchor rewrites
  the live transcript from the session projection, so a relief that
  compacted while the crash-safe persister still had the just-sent
  message in flight re-anchored onto a projection without it (the live
  context silently lost the newest message and the trim valve found
  nothing droppable — the turn died on the guard error instead of
  being relieved). AC: a gated-persist IT-2 fixture holds the newest
  record's append in flight across the relief and asserts the turn
  still completes.
- fix(gh-2096): auto-compact no longer re-pays the judge budget on every
  run when the configured smol class cannot answer within it, and a judge
  timeout no longer kills the retry. Three engine changes: (1) the
  judge call runs under a PER-CALL child cancel token — a budget expiry
  aborts only the in-flight call while the retry and the later LM stages
  keep the run-wide token live (previously the first timeout cancelled
  the shared token and the retry died born-cancelled in ~75 ms); (2) the
  consecutive judge-failure counter is persisted per session as additive
  `structured_judge_health` custom records (newest wins; no migrations —

Judge/smol model-class rule: the `smol` role also serves the structured
compaction hide judge — ONE call under a fixed attempt budget
(`compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds`, default 300 s) with a bounded input
(newest 512 ledger entries). Pick a class that answers within that budget
(a non-mandatory-reasoning class, or a budget sized to the class's
thinking time); a mandatory-reasoning class behind a queueing gateway can
make EVERY judge call hit the full budget. The engine defends itself: a
judge that times out falls back to the deterministic judge-less hide
after two consecutive failures, and the failure latches across runs —
auto-compact then skips the judge (deterministic hide) and pays one
probe call per window instead of the full budget per run. The named
failure line carries the attempt shape (input entries, est. tokens,
elapsed), so a slow-reasoning class reads differently from a wedged
endpoint in logs.

arguments.content:
# Auto-compaction and the trigger tuning

Auto-compaction keeps a long session inside the model's context window by
folding older history into a structured checkpoint summary. This page is
about WHEN it fires — the trigger — and the `compaction:` config keys
that let you move it (gh-2098).

## The trigger model

The trigger evaluates TWO channels at every turn boundary and fires when
either crosses (gh-1742):

- **Estimate channel** — the chars/4 request estimate of the live
  transcript.
- **Observed channel** — the provider-reported accepted context of the
  last completed request (`usage.input + usage.cacheRead`). Observed
  wins: the pressure is `max(estimate, observed)`, and an
  observed-only crossing runs the pass FORCED (the estimate cannot see
  it).

Both channels compare against the same line: `window − reserveTokens`,
where the reserve comes from `CompactionSettings.forWindow(window)` —
the gh-1742 curve:

- `reserve = min(65536, max(window ~/ 16, legacy flat curve))` — 6.25%
  of the window on the proportional band (≥ 262,144), floored by the
  legacy flat 16Ki curve below it. Above 262k the trigger sits at
  **93.75% of the window**; on a 128k window the flat 16Ki reserve puts
  it at 87.2%.
- `keepRecentTokens = min(131072, max(window ~/ 8, legacy curve))` —
  where the context restarts after a pass.

## The tuning keys (gh-2098)

In `~/.fah/config.yaml` (user scope) or `<project>/.fah/config.yaml`
(project scope, wins per key):

```yaml
compaction:
  # Fire when the anchored context reaches 75% of the window.
  triggerRatio: 0.75
  # OR set the headroom directly (mutually exclusive with triggerRatio):
  # reserveTokens: 50000
  # And/or override where the context restarts after a pass:
  # keepRecentTokens: 80000
```

- `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1): the trigger line moves to `r × window`.
  Implemented as `reserve = window − floor(r × window)` — one reserve
  value, so EVERY window-derived consumer moves together: both trigger
  channels, the structured engine's gate and fragile-band escalation,
  the ctx meter, the spill budget, and subagent children (the CLI
  passes the merged section to the task executor).
- `reserveTokens` (positive int): the headroom set directly — the
  forWindow curve's reserve is replaced. `triggerRatio` and
  `reserveTokens` are two spellings of the same knob (the trigger
  line); configuring both is a boot error.
- `keepRecentTokens` (positive int): the post-compaction kept-recent
  region replaces the forWindow curve's.

**Absent keys → byte-identical gh-1742 behavior.** The tuning applies
over the scaled forWindow curve, not instead of it: a ratio overrides
only the trigger line, only a configured `keepRecentTokens` overrides
the keep curve.

Validation is strict (the whole `compaction:` section has been since
issue #148): a mistyped value, a ratio at/below 0 or at/above 1, a
non-positive budget, or the ratio+reserve combination throws a named
`ConfigException` at boot and at `fa config set` — nothing is persisted
that the next boot would reject.

Degenerate-guard note (mirrored from the forWindow curve): a reserve
over half the window (a ratio below ~0.5) clamps to `window ~/ 4`, and
a keep over the window clamps to `window ~/ 2` — a pass must always
free tokens.

Precedence for a run:

1. an explicit full `CompactionSettings` pin (hosts only — no yaml
   surface), with the tuning composed over it;
2. a non-empty `compaction:` tuning — a user pin;
3. the bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) over the forWindow
   curve — it retunes the DEFAULTS for a bench run and never rewrites a
   pinned section (gh-1604).

The Flutter app host does not read the tuning keys yet (it reads only
`compaction.engine` today — the same surface `judgeBudgetSeconds` had
before gh-2098); its wiring stays byte-identically on the forWindow
curve.

## Default decision and the benchmark note

**The legacy curve stays the default.** Absent keys are
byte-identical by contract; moving every session to the 0.75–0.80 band
silently multiplies compaction frequency (each pass is an LLM call on
the summarizer role — cost and latency), and the published Context Rot
curve degrades gracefully, not cliff-edge: the industry band buys
quality on very long sessions, at a measurable frequency price
everywhere. Operators of large-window classes opt in per scope; 0.80
is the informed middle (fires at 80% with a modest frequency increase).

Method (reproduce with your own recorded session — the curve is a
private artifact, the sim is standalone):

```bash
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> \
  --window 128000 --window 200000 --window 400000
# deltas scaled ×3 = an emulated marathon riding the same per-request
# growth shape:
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <session.jsonl> --scale 3 \
  --window 200000 --window 400000
```

The sim replays the recorded per-request observed contexts
(`input + cacheRead`) as a sawtooth: on crossing the policy's line the
context restarts at the keep curve and continues riding the recorded
growth deltas.

Recorded session (218 requests, observed context 19,828 → 178,771;
the gh-1742 anchor channel):

| window | policy | trigger | first fire | fires over the curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128k | legacy (0.9375) | 87.20% | 87.48% | 1 |
| 128k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.21% | 1 |
| 128k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 75.08% | 2 |
| 200k | legacy (0.9375) | 91.81% | never | 0 |
| 200k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.01% | 1 |
| 200k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 75.38% | 1 |
| 400k | legacy (0.9375) | 93.75% | never | 0 |
| 400k | 0.80 | 80.00% | never | 0 |
| 400k | 0.75 | 75.00% | never | 0 |

The same curve with per-request deltas scaled ×3 (an emulated
large-window marathon):

| window | policy | trigger | first fire | fires over the curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200k | legacy (0.9375) | 91.81% | 92.30% | 2 |
| 200k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 84.45% | 3 |
| 200k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 77.11% | 3 |
| 400k | legacy (0.9375) | 93.75% | 93.83% | 1 |
| 400k | 0.80 | 80.00% | 80.25% | 1 |
| 400k | 0.75 | 75.00% | 76.43% | 1 |

Reading: on the recorded session the legacy default never fires at
200k/400k — the session completes inside the window, exactly the
late-fire profile the ticket names; 0.80 fires once at 80% with no
extra passes; 0.75 buys 5 more points of headroom for a doubled pass
count on the 128k class. On the ×3 marathon the frequency cost is
+50% (2 → 3 passes at 200k), not an order of magnitude — the informed
opt-in price.

arguments.newText:
## Unreleased

- feat(gh-2098): the auto-compact trigger is user-configurable —
  `compaction.triggerRatio` / `compaction.reserveTokens` /
  `compaction.keepRecentTokens` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (per-key deepest scope wins) override the gh-1742
  `forWindow` curves; absent keys stay byte-identical (golden-pinned).
  `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1) pins the trigger line at r × window
  (reserve = window − floor(r·window)) so every window-derived consumer
  moves together — both trigger channels (estimate + the gh-1742
  observed anchor), the structured engine's gate and fragile-band
  escalation, the ctx meter, the spill budget, and task children (the
  CLI threads the merged section through the executor). `reserveTokens`
  sets the headroom directly (mutually exclusive with `triggerRatio` —
  strict named `ConfigException`s, also enforced at `fa config set` —
  nothing persists that the next boot would reject); `keepRecentTokens`
  overrides the post-pass kept region. Degenerate guards mirror
  forWindow (reserve > window/2 clamps to window/4, keep > window
  clamps to window/2) so a pass always frees tokens. A non-empty tuning
  is a user pin: the bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`)
  never rewrites it (gh-1604's rule). Default decision documented in
  `docs/compaction.md` with the benchmark note
  (`bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart`, fire points + frequency at
  0.9375 vs 0.80 vs 0.75 on a recorded 218-request session): the legacy
  curve stays the default (byte-identical contract + pass-frequency
  cost), 0.80 is the informed opt-in. Stale doc comment fixed: the CLI
  settings field described a ratio-based default
  ("ratio 0.7, reserve 50000, keep 80000") that never shipped — the
  field now says what it does and points at [compactionTuning].

hit=collections.defaultdict(set); miss=collections.defaultdict(set)
for p in glob.glob('coverage/test/compaction/*.vm.json'):
    d=json.load(open(p))
    for entry in d['coverage']:
        sf=entry.get('source','')
        if '/tuning.dart' not in sf and '/host_wiring.dart' not in sf: continue
        key='tuning.dart' if '/tuning.dart' in sf else 'host_wiring.dart'
        for token in entry['hits']:
            if isinstance(token, list):
                line, hits = token[0], token[-1]
                if line is None or isinstance(line,str): continue
                (hit if hits>0 else miss)[key].add(line)
            else:
                # {line: n, hitCount: n} shape
                line=token.get('line'); hc=token.get('hitCount', token.get('hits',0))
                if line is None: continue
                (hit if hc>0 else miss)[key].add(line)
for k in ('tuning.dart','host_wiring.dart'):
    m=miss[k]-hit[k]; h=hit[k]
    total=len(h|m)
    pct=100*len(h)/total if total else 100
    print(k, f'{len(h)}/{total} covered = {pct:.1f}%')
    print('  uncovered lines:', sorted(m))
EOF

arguments.content:
### What changed
The auto-compact trigger is user-configurable: `compaction.triggerRatio` / `compaction.reserveTokens` / `compaction.keepRecentTokens` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or `.fah/config.yaml` override the gh-1742 `forWindow` curves; absent keys stay byte-identical (golden-pinned). The stale `compactionSettings` doc comment in `agent_cli_config.dart` (a ratio default that never shipped) is fixed.

### Key decisions
- `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1) converts to `reserve = window − floor(r·window)` at the shared host-wiring seam — one reserve value, so every window-derived consumer moves together: both trigger channels (estimate + the gh-1742 observed anchor), the structured engine's gate + fragile-band escalation, the ctx meter, the spill budget, and task children (threaded through `TaskExecutor`).
- `triggerRatio` + `reserveTokens` are mutually exclusive (the ratio already fixes the trigger line) — strict named `ConfigException`s at boot and at `fa config set`; nothing persists that the next boot would reject.
- Per-key scope merge (project wins over user), yaml round-trip via `_compactionYaml`, and a non-empty tuning is a user pin: the bench env knob `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` never rewrites it (gh-1604's rule).
- Default stays the legacy curve — benchmarked in `docs/compaction.md` (`bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart`, fire points + frequency at 0.9375 vs 0.80 vs 0.75 on a recorded 218-request session): on the recorded session legacy never fires at 200k/400k; 0.80 fires once at 80% for no extra passes; 0.75 doubles the pass count on the 128k class.
- Degenerate guards mirror `forWindow` (reserve > window/2 clamps to window/4, keep > window clamps to window/2) so a pass always frees tokens.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction/tuning_test.dart test/compaction/host_wiring_test.dart \
  test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart \
  test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart test/config/config_service_test.dart
dart bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart <recorded-session.jsonl> --window 128000 --window 200000
```

<details><summary>Config flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  YAML["compaction: yaml (user < project, per key)"] --> P["CompactionTuning.fromSection (strict)"]
  P --> M["mergeCompactionTuning"] --> W["resolveCompactionHostWiring"]
  W --> A["applyCompactionTuning over forWindow"] --> S["CompactionSettings"]
  S --> T["shouldCompact (estimate)"] --> FIRE["compact when pressure > line"]
  S --> O["assessContextPressure (observed anchor, forced)"] --> FIRE
  S --> C["task children (TaskExecutor)"] --> FIRE
```

</details>

All green and landed. Final summary:

**gh-2098 — user-configurable auto-compact trigger, complete.**

### What changed
`compaction.triggerRatio` / `compaction.reserveTokens` / `compaction.keepRecentTokens` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project `.fah/config.yaml` now override the gh-1742 `forWindow` curves; absent keys stay byte-identical (golden-pinned). The stale `compactionSettings` doc comment (a ratio default that never shipped) is fixed.

### Key decisions
- `triggerRatio` (0 < r < 1) converts to `reserve = window − floor(r·window)` at the shared host-wiring seam — every window-derived consumer moves together: both trigger channels (estimate + observed anchor), the structured engine's gate + fragile-band escalation, ctx meter, spill budget, and task children (threaded through `TaskExecutor`).
- `triggerRatio` + `reserveTokens` mutually exclusive — strict named `ConfigException`s at boot and `fa config set`; bad values never persist.
- Default stays legacy — benchmarked (`bench/compaction_trigger_sim.dart`, `docs/compaction.md`): on a recorded 218-request session legacy never fires at 200k/400k; 0.80 fires once at 80% for no extra passes; 0.75 doubles pass count at 128k. 0.80 documented as the informed opt-in.
- Degenerate guards mirror `forWindow` so a pass always frees tokens.

### How to verify
`dart test test/compaction/tuning_test.dart test/compaction/host_wiring_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — all green (498 compaction + 4407 cli + 395 task + 98 hosts + 499 session/usage/parity + 17 flutter parity + guards); `dart analyze lib bin` clean; coverage 98.1%/100% on the new files; 6 commits on `ai/gh-2098` ahead of fresh `origin/main` (b762d90).
